author: residuescaling_92893
content: Large operators typically don't control the WC, and even the holders of the WC may be walled behind a custodian who won't support such signatures for a long time (i.e: it took ledger 1 year to support consolidations requests, and some around still don't). It feels like it's more work at an ecosystem level to do this solely via WC, it will slow transition. If there is a BLS path there, big operators can do it faster.

author: ladidan
content: <@1513906114079625449> is bringing up an argument for having the registration message be signed by the validator signing key / operator (as opposed to the withdrawal credentials / allocator or owner), due to the allocator being unable to sign such a message as their custodian does not support it

author: ladidan
content: These custodians, e.g. Fireblocks, Bitgo, Coinbase custody, etc serve as an abstraction layer to the allocators/owners of the stake. So if it were on the latter to register, they'd be dependent on the custodian to have adapted their frontend/API for such a new registration method - which for consolidations took many of them a very long time (some never supported it) which risks migration delays.

author: residuescaling_92893
content: It's also like: big node operator has 50 stakers behind, needs to have a conversation with each of them to convince them, then those have to have the conversation with whoever is in charge of signing/their custodian, etc. While at the end of the day, this rotation is an operator duty that could be done directly
